correctness.rationale: Fix any initial configuration. Independence and finite fields give a full-support product law for the intermediate spins. Conditional covariance of distinct outputs reduces to covariance of their intermediate-state mean functions. When they share a neighbor, both mean functions are strictly increasing in its spin, and nondecreasing in every other spin. Conditioning on the shared spin, the first covariance term is nonnegative by induction on the remaining independent coordinates; the second is strictly positive since both conditional means strictly increase and the shared spin is nondegenerate. If there is no such pair, every vertex has degree one under the graph hypotheses. Its partner map is bijective, so the output coordinates use distinct independent intermediate spins and separate second-step noise. Each binary channel has mean tanh(beta/2) times its input; the composition has mean tanh(beta/2)^2 times the initial spin, giving the asserted parameter. Equality of the two-step kernels extends to the even-time path laws, with the same starting law. The path witness reduces to the shared-spin variance, including the stated rational values.
residual_risks: No claim at beta=0, at infinite beta, or for signed interactions and nonproduct update noise. The finite reproduction supplements the conditional association proof.
